correctness.rationale: Every selected rook vertex is an edge of K_{m,n}; a shortest-path forbidden triple is exactly a selected simple 3-edge path. A bipartite graph lacking such paths has only star components. The labeled two-color exponential formula gives a bijection without double counting 1-edge components. The maximum-set trichotomy follows by forcing exactly two star components; the four-cycle is treated separately. The independent metric-based checker matched the component recurrence on 146762 subsets in 24 small instances. Finite tests corroborate rather than replace the general proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General definitions and universal inclusion-exclusion are not closed family coefficient evaluations. The published total-forest generating data is a coarser invariant: in K_{2,2}, for example, three-edge spanning trees exist but no three-edge star forest. Therefore the full set of rook-general-position coefficients and thin/thick optimizer multiplicities are not direct substitution corollaries of those published scalar or aggregate statements.

originality.rationale: The full two-parameter general-position polynomial and count of all maximizing sets are distinct from the established scalar value in Ghorbani et al. 2019, the path-grid polynomial computations of Irsic et al. 2024, the ascending star-forest decomposition existence theorem of Aroca--Llado 2015, and Stones 2014, which enumerates all forests without singling out star forests. Complete primary texts were compared on matching objects/quantifiers. Targeted current research-index searches supplied no closer theorem; this is not a claim of guaranteed uniqueness.
residual_risks: A prior exact enumeration of two-colored labeled star forests might exist under species, forbidden-path, or bipartite graph-class terminology and imply the same exponential generating function.
Historical databases and informal tables cannot be exhaustively searched, and a failed textual search is not proof of uniqueness.
The scalar maximum-cardinality bound and the C4 special case are known and explicitly excluded from novelty.

value.rationale: The entire cardinality distribution of general-position sets for a natural two-parameter graph class is the primary mathematical object, not a tiny numerical improvement. Its exact compact bivariate exponential generating function bridges metric geodesics and labelled bipartite star forests; the top coefficient counts every extremal set and exhibits a genuine thin/thick boundary. Earlier scalar formulas and all-forest totals do not answer these questions. The work does not assert a general downstream theorem or an arbitrary finite slice.
